headline: AI and deal wins are growing, but muted CC growth and a lower FY2027 outlook warrant a careful reading of the headline INR numbers.

business.summary: A sector-diversified technology-services business whose largest revenue pools remain Financial Services, Manufacturing and Energy/Utilities/Resources.

points.text: The company describes its operations as end-to-end business solutions across Financial Services, Manufacturing, Retail, Energy/Utilities/Resources, Communication, Hi-Tech and Life Sciences.

citations.quote: The Company’s operations predominantly relate to providing end-to-end business solutions to enable clients to enhance performance of their business.
citations.title: INFY Annual Report 2026

citations.title: INFY Annual Report 2026

points.text: Financial Services supplied 28.0% of Q2 FY2027 revenue, Manufacturing 16.0%, and Energy/Utilities/Resources 14.2%; Life Sciences reached 8.4%. These are revenue-mix figures, not segment profit margins.

financial.summary: Q2 FY2027 revenue was ₹ 49,244 crore and owner-attributable PAT ₹ 7,823 crore; reported INR growth materially exceeded constant-currency growth.

points.text: For the quarter ended 30 Sep 2026, revenue was ₹ 49,244 crore, up 10.7%YoY and 2.1%QoQ; PBT was ₹ 11,063 crore, up 8.2%YoY and 0.3%QoQ.

Total consolidated PAT was ₹ 7,838 crore, comprising₹ 7,823 crore attributable to owners and ₹ 15 crore to non-controlling interests. The owner-attributable figure grew 6.2%YoY and 0.7%QoQ; those growth rates must not be applied to total PAT without recalculation.
The company reported 21.0% operating margin for Q2, versus 21.1% in Q1. This is an operating-profit metric; the latest filing does not report it as EBITDA.

citations.quote: Operating profit
citations.title: INFY Outcome of Board Meeting 2026-10-23

limitations: EBITDA is not labelled in the latest results filing. Operating profit is preserved separately.
INR and USD tables, consolidated/standalone statements and quarterly/half-year columns coexist in the source.

trajectory.summary: The three-year INR revenue and profit trend is upward, while the latest constant-currency growth and guidance show slower underlying momentum.

points.text: Consolidated revenue increased from ₹ 153,670 crore in FY2024 to ₹ 162,990 crore in FY2025 and ₹ 178,650 crore in FY2026. Owner-attributable profit moved from ₹ 26,233 crore to ₹ 26,713 crore and ₹ 29,440 crore over those years.

FY2026 INR revenue grew 9.6%, but constant-currency growth was 3.1%. Management also said annual volumes were flattish, with growth led by realization; the INR headline therefore does not imply equivalent volume growth.

points.text: Quarterly CC YoY growth slowed from 2.4% in Q1 FY2027 to 1.5% in Q2, while FY2027 CC guidance moved from 1.5%–3% in July to 1%–2% in October. This is a weaker growth outlook despite continued positive revenue growth.

balance.summary: The March 2026 annual balance sheet reports no outstanding borrowings, substantial liquidity and meaningful lease obligations; working-capital absorption deserves attention.

points.text: At 31 Mar 2026, the annual report states there were no outstanding borrowings and consolidated cash/investments of ₹ 43,075 crore. It says growth has been financed largely through cash generated from operations.

cash.summary: Profits were backed by operating cash, but FY2026 cash conversion softened as cash taxes and working-capital outflows increased.

points.text: Ind-AS operating cash flow was ₹ 33,986 crore in FY2026, versus ₹ 35,694 crore in FY2025 and ₹ 25,210 crore in FY2024. FY2026 CFO covered total PAT of ₹ 29,474 crore by approximately 115.3%, calculated from these source values.

narrative.summary: AI and large deals are becoming material, but current group growth and repeated annual guidance cuts temper the optimistic story.

points.text: Management said AI revenue reached 10.5% of Q2 revenue, growing 29% sequentially, from 8.2% in Q1. Yet group CC growth was only 1.5%YoY in Q2 and FY2027 guidance was reduced to 1%–2%; AI momentum and overall growth therefore tell different parts of the story.

citations.quote: AI revenue was a standout at 10.5% of our revenue, growing at 29% sequentially. And last quarter, it was at 8.2%.
citations.title: INFY Earnings-call transcript Oct 2026

citations.quote: Our revenue growth for Q2 was 1.5% YoY and 1.2% sequentially in constant currency terms.
citations.title: INFY Earnings-call transcript Oct 2026

citations.quote: our revenue growth guidance is 1% to 2% YoY.in constant currency terms.
citations.title: INFY Earnings-call transcript Oct 2026

points.text: The INR revenue increase of 10.7%YoY looks stronger than the 1.5% CC increase. Both are company disclosures; the comparison shows why currency-adjusted growth is necessary when assessing the strength of the underlying narrative.

citations.quote: Our revenue growth for Q2 was 1.5% YoY and 1.2% sequentially in constant currency terms.
citations.title: INFY Earnings-call transcript Oct 2026

points.text: Management explicitly cited softer volumes, competitive pricing and greater productivity demands when explaining the October outlook reduction. These comments provide a concrete counterweight to the strong AI/deal narrative without attributing all weakness to AI.

citations.quote: Our Q2 has been softer and our volume continues to remain softer.
citations.title: INFY Earnings-call transcript Oct 2026

citations.quote: We have also seen pricing pressure on the back of competitive intensity and higher ask on productivity.
citations.title: INFY Earnings-call transcript Oct 2026

limitations: The sources support the contrast; they do not quantify how much of the growth slowdown was caused by any single factor.

guidance.summary: Latest guidance is 1%–2% FY2027 CC revenue growth and 20%–22% operating margin; the year is incomplete, so delivery remains pending.

points.text: At the 23 Oct 2026 call, management guided FY2027 CC revenue growth of 1%–2% and operating margin of 20%–22%. These are annual expectations, not promises for the next individual quarter.

points.text: The FY2027 revenue band was 1.5%–3.5% in April and 1.5%–3% in July before the October reduction. Track this change in expectations separately from the eventual full-year outcome.

bullBear.summary: Bull case: monetising AI, large-deal wins and strong cash backing. Bear case: muted underlying growth, pricing pressure and repeated guidance reductions.

points.text: Bull case—an inference from disclosures: AI at 10.5% of revenue and Q2 large deals of$5.2 billion could support future revenue if they convert as expected; these signings are not current-period revenue.

citations.quote: AI revenue was a standout at 10.5% of our revenue
citations.title: INFY Earnings-call transcript Oct 2026

citations.quote: Large deals were another standout at $5.2 bn for the quarter.
citations.title: INFY Earnings-call transcript Oct 2026

points.text: Bull case—cash resilience: the annual report discloses no outstanding borrowings, substantial cash/investments and FY2026 CFO above total PAT. This provides financial flexibility, while retaining the separate lease-liability caveat.

citations.quote: We have no outstanding borrowings.
citations.title: INFY Annual Report 2026

citations.quote: Consolidated cash and investments of ₹43,075 crore
citations.title: INFY Annual Report 2026

citations.quote: Net cash generated by operating activities 33,986 35,694
citations.title: INFY Annual Report 2026

citations.quote: Profit for the year 29,474 26,750
citations.title: INFY Annual Report 2026

points.text: Bear case—group CC growth of 1.5%YoY, pricing pressure and a cut in annual guidance to 1%–2% indicate that strong AI/deal activity has not yet translated into broad-based acceleration. FY2026 CFO also declined despite profit growth.

scorecard.promise: Prior 16Oct 2025 guidance: FY2026 CC revenue growth 2%–3%; an annual horizon.
scorecard.actual: Q3 CC revenue grew 1.7%YoY and 0.6%QoQ. At the 14Jan 2026 release, full-year delivery was still pending and guidance was revised to 3%–3.5%.
scorecard.rationale: Historical assessment at the Q3 release: the earlier annual promise cannot be graded using one quarter. The completed FY2026 outcome is assessed in the Q4 row.
